correctness.rationale: Cycle suppression proves the forest criterion. Every external subdivision vertex must be included; the internal selected subdivisions form spanning trees of original induced components; a missing original vertex can be added without forming a cycle exactly when it has no two neighbors in the same such component. These are biconditional proofs including boundary and disconnected cases. Specialization to K_n and Cayley enumeration yield the full polynomial; checked exact first difference yields all extremal claims. Independent brute-force code passed on 76 graphs / 44,662 subsets / 555 facets.

value.rationale: The result characterizes all inclusion-maximal induced forests for arbitrary full graph subdivisions and yields a complete natural closed combinatorial classification for subdivided cliques. It determines the entire cardinality distribution of inclusion-minimal feedback vertex sets, both extremal sizes and multiplicities, permanent nonpurity from four originals onward, and unbounded gaps. These are meaningful exact invariants and structural phenomena beyond the known scalar minimum, rather than arbitrary small numerical slices.
